Subject: Attestation request — ephemeral-runner timeline + emergency change authority

Hi Nikhil,

Thanks for taking this on. The assessor (Tom Hargreaves) has a couple of focused asks while we complete the SIG/SOC2 intake:

1) A short written attestation describing how ephemeral CI runners are provisioned and retired (including sampling of logs showing creation -> action -> teardown for three recent changes).
2) The documented emergency-change authority matrix (who can approve a hotfix outside normal change windows) and a recent example (ticket number or succinct chronology) where the emergency flow was used.
3) Any redaction guidance you used when producing logs for external assessors.

Can you provide the attestation + artifacts by Tue EOD (US-PST)? If something needs additional redaction or a POA&M, flag it in your response.

Appreciate the quick turnaround — we’re trying to close the assessor’s open items this sprint.

Best,
Marta
Marta Ruiz
Security Programs, Atlas Bank

Attachments: none
From: Nikhil Sharma <nikhil.sharma@redwoodinference.com>
To: Marta Ruiz <marta.ruiz@atlasbank.com>
Cc: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwoodinference.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwoodinference.com>, Tom Hargreaves <tom.h@thirdparty-audit.io>
Date: Mon, 16 Dec 2024 11:02:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Attestation request — ephemeral-runner timeline + emergency change authority

Hi Marta / Tom,

Thanks — we can provide this. Summary of what I’m attaching and the plan:

- emergency-change-authority-matrix.pdf: current roster and approval thresholds (signed by VP Engineering).
- ephemeral-runner-sampling-20241214.csv: ten-event sampling showing runner create/pull/execute/teardown markers (timestamps + runner-id).
- redacted-ephemeral-logs-20241214.txt: example of a runner lifecycle from our GitHub Actions -> internal orchestration -> teardown, with IPs and developer emails redacted per our standard policy.

Short attestation (below) is included inline; you’ll find the full artifacts in the Drive link I’ll share in a follow-up. If you need a longer formal attestation on company letterhead we can escalate to Legal/Compliance.

--- Attestation (engineer-authoritative) ---
Redwood Inference attests that ephemeral CI runners are programmatically provisioned by our build orchestration service, executed with time-limited credentials, and automatically deprovisioned after job completion or after 90 minutes of inactivity. Specific safeguards in place:
- Runners are created in a restricted subnet and assigned ephemeral role credentials scoped to the job.
- Logs record runner lifecycle events (CREATE, START, FINISH, DELETE) with UTC timestamps, runner-id, job-id, and anonymized user-id.
- Secrets required for build steps are fetched from an internal secrets service with short TTLs and are never persisted to runner disk in cleartext.
- We retain runner lifecycle logs for ninety (90) days for operational and audit purposes; access is logged and requires role-based approval.

Signed,
Nikhil Sharma
Senior Security Engineer, Redwood Inference
--- end attestation ---

Notes and callouts:
- Emergency change authority: our emergency matrix allows Director+Engineering to approve a production hotfix; VP Engineering or Security signs off for cross-region rollouts. The attached PDF contains a sample chronology (internal ticket RF-20241208-HOTFIX) where the flow was used and later reviewed in the weekly change retrospective.
- Redaction policy: IP addresses and full email addresses are replaced with hash tokens (sha256 prefix) in artifacts produced for external assessors; user identifiers are replaced with role tags (e.g., developer-frontend-1). We included a redaction summary file inside the Drive folder.

Next steps: I’ll upload the three artifacts to the shared Drive and share a link + minimal DOA (document of attestation) by this afternoon. If you want a one-page cover letter on letterhead, CC Legal (Olga) and we’ll route.

Regards,
Nikhil

Attachments: ephemeral-runner-sampling-20241214.csv (sample), emergency-change-authority-matrix.pdf (matrix), redacted-ephemeral-logs-20241214.txt (example)

Marta / Tom,

Quick note from Legal/Compliance: the attestation draft Nikhil provided is fine for initial intake. A couple of clarifying asks for the assessor: please confirm

1) Whether any shared secrets (e.g., cloud account keys) are ever exfiltrated to ephemeral runners — answer: no, secrets are tokenized and ephemeral credentials are fetched per-job.
2) Confirm who reviewed the emergency ticket RF-20241208-HOTFIX and the date of the retrospective — answer: reviewed by Director of Engineering (Laura Bennett) on 2024-12-10; minutes attached in the matrix PDF.

If Atlas requires our CISO-signed letter, we’ll prepare that; it may take 24-48 hours. For now, please proceed with the link to the Drive artifacts.

Thanks,
Olga Petrov
